source.title: Attention Is All You Need
source.date_note: The original arXiv submission was 2017-06-12; the current arXiv record is v7 revised 2023-08-02. This case preserves the paper's original sequence-transduction/machine-translation context rather than projecting later decoder-only LLM developments back into the 2017 claims.

inspection.method: Direct inspection of the arXiv abstract and paper PDF, especially the architecture/attention sections, positional encoding, Table 1 / Why Self-Attention, and machine-translation results.
gaps: This case does not reconstruct every attention equation, optimization setting or later Transformer variant.
The paper's 2017 WMT BLEU/training results are historical evidence for the proposed architecture, not a ranking of current language models.

prior_knowledge.query: Understand why self-attention replaced recurrence for the Transformer architecture, what parallelism and dependency modeling changed, and which claims belong to the original machine-translation context rather than later LLM folklore.

content_map.problem: Dominant sequence-transduction models used recurrent or convolutional encoder-decoder networks, which introduced sequential computation and longer paths between distant sequence positions.
content_map.thesis: The Transformer removes recurrence and convolution and uses attention-based encoder-decoder layers so all positions can interact through self-attention, reducing sequential operations and dependency path length while making sequence order an explicit positional-encoding input.
mechanisms: Each encoder position can attend to all positions in the previous encoder layer through self-attention.
The decoder uses masked self-attention so a position cannot attend to later output positions, preserving autoregressive generation.
Encoder-decoder attention lets decoder queries attend to encoder representations.
Removing recurrence means layer computation across known sequence positions no longer requires O(n) recurrent sequential steps.
All-to-all self-attention gives constant maximum path length between positions but has O(n²·d) per-layer complexity in the paper's comparison.
Positional encodings inject token order because the model contains neither recurrence nor convolution.
examples: English constituency parsing as a second task family
claims: The 2017 Transformer is an encoder-decoder sequence-transduction model based solely on attention rather than recurrence or convolution.
Self-attention reduces the minimum sequential operations per layer from O(n) for recurrence to O(1) and the maximum dependency path from O(n) to O(1), according to the paper's Table 1.
That path/parallelism advantage comes with O(n²·d) self-attention complexity, so the paper itself treats sequence length as a trade-off and discusses restricted attention for very long sequences.
Positional encodings are required to inject order because the architecture removes recurrence and convolution.
The decoder remains autoregressive by masking future positions; attention-only layers do not make output generation fully parallel.

The paper's reported quality and training-time evidence comes primarily from WMT 2014 machine translation and should not be generalized into a current claim about every later Transformer/LLM architecture.
evidence: arXiv abstract identifies the architecture and WMT translation results.
PDF §3 describes encoder self-attention, masked decoder self-attention and encoder-decoder attention.
PDF §3.5 states positional information is added because the model has no recurrence or convolution.
PDF Table 1 / §4 compares complexity, sequential operations and maximum path length for self-attention, recurrent and convolutional layers.
assumptions: The task is sequence transduction with sequence representations available for parallel layer computation during training/encoding.
Token order must be represented explicitly once recurrence/convolution no longer supplies an ordering bias.
The paper's computational comparison uses sequence length n and representation dimension d and does not imply self-attention is cheapest at every sequence length.
limitations: Self-attention's all-pairs interaction has O(n²·d) per-layer complexity in sequence length, so constant path length is not free for long contexts.
The original Transformer is an encoder-decoder sequence-transduction architecture, not the later decoder-only LLM template that dominates many current language models.
Masked decoder self-attention preserves autoregressive output dependence, so the paper's O(1) sequential-operations layer comparison should not be read as fully parallel autoregressive generation.

The WMT 2014 BLEU and training-time results are historical evidence from the paper's tasks/hardware rather than universal evidence that attention-only models outperform every recurrent or convolutional architecture today.
open_questions: How later long-context architectures changed the quadratic self-attention cost while preserving useful dependency paths.
Which later developments made decoder-only Transformers the dominant LLM architecture rather than the original encoder-decoder design.

selection.requested_focus: Understand why self-attention replaced recurrence for the Transformer architecture, what parallelism and dependency modeling changed, and which claims belong to the original machine-translation context rather than later LLM folklore.
coherent_core: Replace recurrent/convolutional sequence layers with attention-based encoder-decoder layers.
Self-attention removes the O(n) recurrent layer dependency chain and gives a constant maximum path between sequence positions.
The parallelism/path advantage trades against quadratic all-pairs attention cost as sequence length grows.
Removing recurrence/convolution makes positional information an explicit input rather than an implicit architectural ordering mechanism.
The original evidence is sequence transduction—especially WMT 2014 translation—not a retrospective claim about all later LLMs.
drop_notes: Do not teach modern decoder-only LLM architecture as though it were the exact 2017 model.
Do not interpret Table 1's O(1) sequential operations as fully parallel autoregressive generation.
All automatically retrieved prior concepts are cross-domain noise and remain suppressed.
connections: ReAct and controlled execution are later agent/runtime layers and should not be graph-linked to the 2017 model architecture merely because both involve attention or sequence decisions.
Modern LLM architecture is a future follow-up source, not evidence retroactively attributed to this paper.

verification_candidates.question: Which later paper should define the transition from the original encoder-decoder Transformer to decoder-only language modeling?
verification_candidates.reason: That evolution is central to modern LLM understanding but is outside the 2017 paper's source claims.

verification_candidates.question: Which long-context attention variants materially alter the O(n²) sequence-length cost while preserving useful global dependencies?
verification_candidates.reason: This is the main technical boundary exposed by the original Table 1 model.
